A · A sign-in section in Manage

Recommended Full story

Manage carries the sign-in: a "Sign in again" section at the top while the plan needs one, the same steps last and titled "Replace sign-in" while it is healthy.

Pros and risks

Pros

  • One place for every plan control: Manage already holds Leasing, Limits, Lends, Voice it, Name.
  • The card stays as it is: one Manage control; the state chip already says Sign-in needed.
  • Lends are on screen in the same sheet while signing in, and after it.

Risks

  • On a healthy plan the section is last: reached by scrolling the sheet.
  • Manage grows by one section; on a phone the needs-sign-in case pushes Leasing below the fold.

B · A Sign in button on the card

Full story

A "Sign in" button on the card of a plan that needs a sign-in opens its own sheet; Manage carries the same entry ("Replace sign-in") for a healthy plan.

Pros and risks

Pros

  • The fix is one press from the list, beside the Sign-in needed chip.
  • The sign-in sheet is short and single-purpose; lends kept are listed in it.

Risks

  • A second control on the card breaks the cards rule of one Manage control (LlmPlans.tsx header comment).
  • A new sheet kind with Back to Manage: one more path to keep in step with Add plan.
  • Two entries (card and Manage) for one action.

C · Add plan recognises the label

Full story

No new control: typing an existing plan's label into Add plan turns the sheet into "Sign in again" (or "Replace sign-in") for that plan, its vendor fixed and its lends sent back.

Pros and risks

Pros

  • Nothing new on cards or in Manage.
  • Matches what the state tooltip already says: sign it in again under the same label.

Risks

  • Hidden: nobody finds it unless they know to type the label.
  • A typo adds a second plan instead of fixing the first.
  • A borrower typing a lent label gets a separate plan in its own workspace: needs its own warning (frame 5).
  • Add plan changes meaning mid-typing; Max agents disappears because the plan keeps its own.
